survivors.claim: The HEAD commit of the range deletes the single-quoted @import arm from stylesheetTargets, so `@import '...'` yields no target and `@import url('...')` yields the garbage target "url" — contradicting D2/Contracts, which name both forms as stylesheet targets.
survivors.impact: A page that applies the gray register or its token sheet through a single-quoted CSS import is read as applying nothing: the atlas refuses a correctly styled page as missing its tokens, the theme composer accepts a candidate that still renders gray, and the journey-drawn closure refuses a drawn wireframe.
survivors.evidence: Spec D2 names the forms @import "...", @import '...', @import url(...), @import url("..."), @import url('...'). Violating hunk: importRe lost the '([^']*)' alternative and the m[2]/m[3] selection collapsed. Executed against HEAD lib: "<style>@import 'e.css';</style>" -> [] false; "<style>@import url('g.css');</style>" -> ["url"] false; "<style>@import url('../../wire/tokens.css');</style>" -> ["url"] false. Real entrypoint: node spec/scripts/design-atlas.js check <mock> on a labeled sketch whose only token sheet is <style>@import '../wire/tokens.css';</style> -> exit 1, CHECK FAIL does not link a tokens.css; the same page with the double-quoted import -> exit 0 CHECK PASS.

survivors.claim: The gate leg is red at HEAD: plugin-bump.js --check fails for the spec plugin, and AC-20260908-07-14 declares [oracle: gate], so the ac-matrix leg emits a HARD oracle-red finding.
survivors.impact: The version-bump oracle this spec's last acceptance criterion relies on is failing, so the suite and gate are both red.
survivors.evidence: Executed node scripts/plugin-bump.js --check -> spec: spec/ changed since 8d88691 but version is 7.114.0 (base 7.114.0), exit=1. Manifest gate exit 1, suite exit 1 (1380 pass / 1 fail: AC-20260908-01-1), ac-matrix exit 1 with HARD oracle-red-or-absent AC-20260908-07-14.

survivors.claim: The range as handed looks wrong: main already merged and closed this exact spec CLEAN at the range's first commit, and the worktree is a detached HEAD carrying two further commits on top of that merged state.
survivors.impact: This review is judging work that has already shipped plus post-merge edits that diverge from what landed.
survivors.evidence: git log --graph --oneline main shows the merge, close and feat commits; git show main:specs/20260908/07-one-wire-register-predicate.md reports status done; git branch -a --contains reports no branch.

survivors.claim: D2's promise of @import '...' and @import url('...') as stylesheet targets is carried by AC-20260908-07-1, but the AC-1 table test asserts neither single-quoted form, so the cited test does not deliver that part of the decision.
survivors.impact: Two of the five import spellings the decision guarantees have no pin, so they can be silently dropped from the shared predicate without any test turning red.
survivors.evidence: Test table lines 38-40 carry only the double-quoted, bare url() and double-quoted url() rows; grep for a single-quoted @import across the test corpus returns nothing. Executed node --test tests/consistency/wire-register.test.js -> pass 7 / fail 0 despite the regression.

survivors.claim: The deviations file's first entry records handleJourneyDrawn calling ensureJourneyRecord + saveStatus() before the per-label loop, but a later commit reverted that change and the net diff no longer contains it.
survivors.impact: A reader of the deviations record will believe the journey-drawn mark writes a stub record before validation when it does not.
survivors.evidence: The revert commit removes the six lines from handleJourneyDrawn; grep at HEAD shows ensureJourneyRecord only on the success path.
